title: The Comprehensive Risk Management Framework
summary: How an infrastructure builds an integrated framework covering credit, liquidity, operational, business, custody and investment risk, and the role of the second and third lines in testing that it works.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How an infrastructure builds an integrated framework covering credit, liquidity, operational, business, custody and investment risk, and the role of the second and third lines in testing that it works.
Learning Objectives: Design an integrated risk framework, appetite and policies across all risk types
Organise the risk, compliance and internal audit functions for an infrastructure
Manage general business, custody and investment risk and the capital to cover them
Syllabus: Risk appetite, policies and model governance
Independent risk, compliance and internal audit functions
General business risk, custody and investment risk
Intended Audience: Board members, risk and audit committee members and senior executives of trading venues, CCPs, CSDs, payment systems and trade repositories
Chief risk officers, heads of compliance, internal audit and risk, treasury, default management and operations staff
Regulatory affairs, legal and strategy teams preparing for supervisory assessments or new services
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Experience of trading, clearing, settlement or payment systems is helpful. No prior study of the PFMI is required.
Core Reading: CPMI-IOSCO, Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (2012)
FSB, Key Attributes of Effective Resolution Regimes for Financial Institutions (2014)
IOSCO, Regulatory Issues Raised by Changes in Market Structure (2013)
FSB, Effective Practices for Cyber Incident Response and Recovery (2020)
